headline: High-risk Dify→python-cheatsheet pairing is mostly blocked, but Dify’s broad write/network defaults create medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure if outputs are reused.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files and use broad network egress, so if it ingests content from the python-cheatsheet side through shared workspace or copied outputs, instruction-like text could be treated as trusted. The cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot actively inject, so the risk is one-way and depends on Dify’s ingestion path.
conditions: IF Dify ingests content from a shared file or pasted document produced from python-cheatsheet
IF an operator treats documentation text as executable instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of external text into Dify prompts
Add a manual review step before copying content into workflows
Restrict Dify workspace access to trusted files only
Use a provenance label for imported documentation
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction-stripping before prompt assembly

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs and knowledge-base files, and its broad network egress plus model-provider/tool credentials mean sensitive content can leave the local workspace when processed. python-cheatsheet itself has no filesystem or network surface, so it is not a leak source; the exposure is from Dify handling shared data classes without isolation.
conditions: IF conversation logs or knowledge-base files contain secrets or regulated data
IF Dify sends those contents to external model providers or tools
mitigations: Remove secrets from uploaded knowledge-base files
Limit Dify projects to non-sensitive data
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
Review provider/tool routing for sensitive prompts
requires-engineering: enforce per-dataset redaction before inference

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no meaningful write-write overlap: Dify can write the filesystem, but python-cheatsheet cannot read or write files, spawn processes, or modify state. That makes direct capability conflict unlikely; any conflict would require an unusual external bridge not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable directory
IF python-cheatsheet is wrapped with additional write permissions not shown here
mitigations: Keep the cheatsheet agent read-only
Separate working directories per agent
Avoid shared mutable git or filesystem state
Document any added write permissions before deployment

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate workflow outputs that downstream systems may treat as authoritative, while python-cheatsheet is a reference source that may be copied into those outputs. If Dify’s output is reused without verification, errors can cascade into later actions or documents; the cheatsheet cannot verify or correct them automatically.
conditions: IF Dify output is forwarded into another workflow step without human review
IF python-cheatsheet text is used as a factual source for Dify-generated actions
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Dify outputs
Add citation checks for any sourced claims
Mark python-cheatsheet as reference-only in prompts
Compare outputs against a second source before execution
requires-engineering: add verification gates between generation and action

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so a compliance breach is not established. The only concrete compliance-relevant difference is that Dify handles conversation logs and knowledge-base content, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes, so the pair’s compliance risk is limited unless sensitive data is introduced into Dify.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Dify
IF Dify retention or logging settings are incompatible with that data class
mitigations: Avoid uploading regulated data to Dify
Set short retention for conversation logs
Review Dify logging settings
Use non-sensitive test content for workflows
